items.title: Cognition shipped a cheaper frontier coding model
items.oneliner: Cognition says SWE-2 hits 50.0% on FrontierCode 1.1 at 64% lower cost, pushing coding model pricing down.

items.title: Inception pushed inference speed into a new tier
items.oneliner: Mercury 2.5 claims 1,100 tokens per second and 40% higher intelligence, making latency a real product differentiator.

items.title: Magic claims a pretraining efficiency breakthrough
items.oneliner: Magic says its recipe cuts pretraining compute by over 10x, which matters more than another benchmark screenshot.

items.title: Meta launched a consumer personal agent
items.oneliner: Meta's Muse handles email, trips, and price tracking, signaling agents are moving from demos into daily workflows.

items.title: Microsoft patched a record vulnerability wave
items.oneliner: Microsoft fixed 972 flaws this month, including 112 critical ones, reminding every AI stack it still runs on brittle software.

items.title: Anthropic exit sharpened the self-improving AI debate
items.oneliner: A departing Anthropic researcher warned about self-improving AI risk, giving policymakers fresh ammunition for tighter controls.

items.title: Rust became a top-tier Microsoft language
items.oneliner: Microsoft elevated Rust to Tier-1 status, a strong signal memory safety is finally becoming a platform requirement.

items.title: PlanetScale introduced sharded Postgres for hyperscale
items.oneliner: PlanetScale's Neki promises real Postgres sharding with online resharding, targeting teams that have outgrown single-node databases.

items.title: Shopify moved back to native mobile development
items.oneliner: Shopify ditched React Native for Swift and Kotlin, arguing LLMs erased much of cross-platform's original labor advantage.

items.title: Google made a massive Finland infrastructure bet
items.oneliner: Google's $15.1 billion Finland investment shows AI competition is now constrained as much by power and land as models.
